# Structural locality eligibility stage

**Build-only handoff.** This stage has no browser page run, structural schedule, runtime counters, or physical change. It tests whether authored stateful/effectful keyed collection TSX lowers through the actual Rust/OXC Vite plugin, whether a native state-array oracle and React Compiler fixture compile, and whether unsupported indexed collection mapping gives the explicit diagnostic. A successful build is **not** proof that the VDOM delta path runs; that needs a later, separately reviewed headless output/protocol gate.

The original proposal and source manifest are copied as `preserved-proposal.md` and `preserved-source-manifest.json`; both the originals and copies are included in `input-lock.json`. The lock also includes fixture, config, gate, compiler source/Cargo lock, relevant live runtime source, package lock and root Vite config. The live VDOM hash belongs to the adjacent-token worktree, distinct from the archived dense qualification. No archived dense speed or path eligibility is inherited.

## Exact Luna command after primary review

From the repository root, run this one-shot build gate with `login:false` and Node `/Users/tjw/.nvm/versions/node/v24.18.0/bin/node`:

```sh
/Users/tjw/.nvm/versions/node/v24.18.0/bin/node .cache/structural-locality-protocol-v1/eligibility/run-build-gates.mjs
```

The script verifies all locked inputs before/after, invokes `cargo build --frozen` in a fresh isolated target under this stage, records the binary hash, builds the positive fixture with local Vite config using the public composed `nativeModulePlugin`, captures emitted native/React source, requests Rust/OXC plans directly from the same binary, verifies compiler plan sites and React memo caches, builds the intentional negative fixture expecting a nonzero diagnostic, and records all local build file hashes, including HTML/maps. It writes `build-gate-report.json` plus separate stdout/stderr logs; failures remain inspectable and return nonzero. It refuses to overwrite any prior report, proof, build or target directory; preserve and review a failed attempt before preparing a new named attempt. The Vite builds do not start a listening server, so Portless is not involved. The stage uses installed Vite/React dependencies and explicitly points the native plugin to the just-built Rust binary. Cargo uses the repository's existing `.cache/cargo` dependency cache in offline mode, while the isolated target forces a full rebuild that may be costly. A cached binary from another source revision is never selected. The report records compiler source root, target path, Cargo home/lock and binary SHA; the static lock records all Rust source and plugin hashes. If a dependency/toolchain prevents the fresh build, report that limitation and do not substitute an unproven cached executable.

Expected positive proof: `NativeRow` has state/effect sites, `NativeCollectionBoard` has one collection site with `requires_owner_render:false`, `GenericRow` has state/effect sites, `NativeGenericBoard` has state and no collection site, and both React components have memo cache calls in the emitted transform. These are **expected**, not preverified. The stateful row remains intact even if a compiler or runtime guard declines delta. Expected negative diagnostic: `native collection .map requires one inline, synchronous, one-parameter arrow callback returning JSX; index parameters and thisArg are unsupported` (exact compiler text retained in the gate).

Public authoring example: construct `const rows = makeRows(ids)`, mount `<NativeCollectionBoard rows={rows} life={life} />`, and edit via `rows.apply(rows.version, [{ type: "move", key: "row-0", beforeKey: null }])` followed by the native root's public `flush()`. `life` records row mount/cleanup; retained row selection uses its real click handler and local `useState`. The generic and React boards accept `registerIdsSetter`, which must return the exact unregistration callback for effect cleanup. No runtime controller or timed interaction is included in this stage.

Primary must inspect emitted plan/code, compiler diagnostics, report input/binary/asset hashes and any failure before authorizing a single headless runtime path gate. Built asset hashes are not yet served-asset hashes; a later Portless page gate must compare served bytes before making runtime claims. The proposed seed `0x5b2026` is only a label here; no random or full matrix schedule is executed.
